shortName: Medical University of South Carolina College of Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The MUSC College of Medicine PRIME Division offers nationally recognized programs to support underrepresented students pursuing a career in medicine. We aim to create an environment that fosters cultural understanding, cultural competency, and opportunities for all backgrounds. 

We offer programs and initiatives to support students from varied backgrounds interested in pursuing a career in medicine, including students with disabilities, those from rural backgrounds, first-generation college students, those from disadvantaged or marginalized backgrounds, and other students interested in addressing health disparities in the communities they serve.  

Our different pathway programs are as follows:

Students Mentors and Mentees in Medicine (SM3)
Summer Institute
Summer Medicine Academy
Post-Baccalaureate Reapplication Program (PREP)

https://medicine.musc.edu/about/pathways-engagement
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students who undergo academic, personal, or health problems while in medical school are granted a leave of absence.  Prior to taking the LOA,  students work with the Student Affairs Dean to create an academic plan that will ensure academic success upon reentry into medical school.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
At MUSC, there are more than 100 student organizations, societies, leadership roles, and ways to get involved. Whether you're looking to connect with others who share your passion, step into a leadership role, or explore new interests, you'll find your path here. From academic and professional societies to service-based groups and interprofessional initiatives, our student organizations reflect our student body's energy, purpose, and creativity. 

https://education.musc.edu/about/offices-services/education-innovation-student-life/student-engagement
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
MUSC is an 82 acre medical complex located in the heart of historic Charleston, SC. This city combines the best that life has to offer: historic homes, art, music, museums, libraries, restaurants, beaches, and some of the country's finest golf courses. 

Within a short walk from Charleston's main street are all the hospitals, research centers, clinical, and basic science buildings that make up the MUSC medical district.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Though on-campus housing is not provided, the MUSC Office of Student Programs maintains an online listing of affordable housing near the MUSC campus. Staff is available to guide students in finding housing in their preferred locations and price range. Please visit the MUSC Housing webpage for insight into off-campus housing and apartments near campus.
 
For more information, please visit www.mymuschousing.com
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The MUSC Student Alliance for Equality (SAFE) is an organization of students of all orientations and identities at MUSC designed to provide a sense of community, support, empowerment and advocacy for anyone whose real or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, or alliance may put them in an at-risk minority group. Our organization works to assist all students in improving their professional education at MUSC regarding sexual and gender minority issues. We also strive to educate policymakers, professionals and educators about the importance of these issues and participate in events that offer its members community service experience in ways that directly benefit LGBTQ+ people and their families. We meet monthly and sponsor events periodically through the academic year.

https://musc.campuslabs.com/engage/organization/safe
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
The MUSC Alliance for Disability Advocacy is a student organization with a mission to foster a coalition of students who are dedicated to improving the accessibility and representation of the disabled community in all fields of healthcare through advocacy initiatives, education, community engagement, and service.

We strive to create a safe space for open dialogue about disability issues, both seen and unseen, with the goal of creating a mutually supportive community. We strive to increase transparency and accessibility by sharing information and experiences relevant to navigating the curricula, disability services, accommodations, and national licensing organizations for students with disabilities. We advocate for students with disabilities with the goal of reducing barriers and supporting students’ health and well-being.

https://musc.campuslabs.com/engage/organization/ada
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Student Wellness Program for the MUSC College of Medicine exists to cultivate a culture of wellness and increase student’s productivity by empowering individuals to be self-managers of their health. Our program is designed to promote the well-being and resiliency of our medical students.

https://medicine.musc.edu/programs/doctor-medicine/student-life/wellness

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The MUSC Center for Academic Excellence and Writing Center offers academic support through learning style assessments, study skills workshops, academic advising for individuals and groups.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interactions very early in the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lectures, Small Groups, Team Based Learning, and Labs
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Rotations in year 3 occur at MUSC, with the exception of Family Medicine, which is completed in a rural county in SC. Rotations in year 4 may be taken away from MUSC at various hospitals in the US.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: The Getting Integrated and Fully Transitioned (GIFT) into medical school program is designed to support the academic and social challenges of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: The College of Medicine does not rank students.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lecture attendance is strongly encouraged but is not mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The FLEX curriculum merges basic science concepts with active clinical application. The Pre-Clerkship phase is designed in organ system blocks and blends normal and abnormal to teach the spectrum of human health and disease. Students engage in early hospital, community, and simulation setting experiences. In FLEX phase, students choose a pathway that best meets their educational needs, professional interests and career aspirations. The following pathways are available: research, humanities, or global health. Eligible students may apply for an accelerated pathway for earlier graduation and entry into a residency position at MUSC. The Immersion phase is comprised of clerkships in family medicine, internal medicine, neurology, OB/GYN, pediatrics, psychiatry, and surgery. 3 selectives are chosen for additional immersion. Enrichment phase is comprised of advanced clinical rotations, electives, and the internship 101 course designed to prepare students for the transition to residency.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
At MUSC College of Medicine, all third-year medical students are required to complete the family medicine rotation in a rural or underserved area of the state.

In addition, the MUSC AnMed Clinical Campus is an option for students interested in pursing Primary Care. Students in this program complete their third and fourth years of medical school at the MUSC AnMed campus located in Anderson, SC. For more information visit: https://medicine.musc.edu/programs/doctor-medicine/anmed-campus
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
As South Carolina's only comprehensive academic health center, MUSC values research as an essential component in our overall mission to preserve and optimize human life in South Carolina and beyond, and provide an environment that promotes learning, discovery and healing.

MUSC COM medical students have a wide variety of research opportunities throughout the curriculum. The Medical Student Research Portal (MSRP) is a centralized portal for students to navigate research and funding opportunities and learn how to engage in a research project. 

The Summer Undergraduate Research Program (SURP) is available for undergraduate students. The program is offered through the MUSC College of Graduate Studies.  Information can be found on the Graduate Studies website at:  https://gradstudies.musc.edu/programs/pathway/summer-undergraduate-research-program.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students participate in volunteer activities by integrating classroom learning with community experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText:
A high percentage of medical students engage in  research. Please visit the MUSC COM Research & Innovation homepage:

https://medicine.musc.edu/research-innovation
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals:
The MUSC AnMed Clinical Campus allows students to complete 3rd and 4th years of medical school at MUSC AnMed located in Anderson, SC. 

https://medicine.musc.edu/programs/doctor-medicine/anmed-campus
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pre-clerkship grades are Pass and Fail. Clinical grades are Honors, High Pass, Pass and Fail.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The Medical University of South Carolina's College of Medicine is leading the way in all areas of the MUSC mission – medical education, patient care, and biomedical research – at our main campus in downtown Charleston and across the state.  Founded in 1824, MUSC is the largest and oldest academic medical center in South Carolina, we serve a diverse group of more than 740 medical students, 850 trainees in residency and fellowship programs, and patients throughout our state and beyond.

As the oldest medical school in the South, MUSC educates more than 3,200 students in six colleges – Dental Medicine, Graduate Studies, Health Professions, Medicine, Nursing, and Pharmacy.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The MUSC College of Medicine is committed to developing outstanding physicians who will deliver the highest quality patient care with compassion and professionalism. Our students are equipped to be exemplary members of interprofessional teams and address complex needs of diverse populations. The educators and leaders at MUSC are committed to the advancement of scientific discovery, teaching and learning, and diversity and inclusion. MUSC graduates are highly competitive for matching into residencies and fellowships at prestigious institutions across the nation in a wide variety of specialties.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: All accepted applicants to the MUSC COM will be subject to a criminal background check. Offers of admission are contingent upon satisfactory criminal background investigation results.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Letters of recommendation must be submitted through the AMCAS Letters Service by using AMCAS Letter Writer Application, Interfolio, mail and/or VirtualEvals. Please ensure all letters are submitted to AMCAS through one or more of the above mediums. Only letters submitted through this service will be included in your application for review by our admissions committee. The Office of Admissions does not accept or process letters of recommendation outside of your AMCAS application.

Please note, unofficial letters of recommendation are not permitted. Only Letters of Recommendation submitted through an applicant’s AMCAS application will be considered.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Letters of recommendation provide personal insight and depth to your character, professionalism, communication skills, work ethic, enthusiasm for medicine, etc. Applicants may submit a maximum of 5 letters of recommendation (LOR) with a  minimum of three.  If your undergraduate institution prepares a Pre-Health or Pre-Medical Advisory Committee letter or packet, this will fulfill the minimum letter requirement.

Applicants without a premed committee packet should include at least one letter from a faculty member (preferably a science faculty member) who instructed you and at least two letters from other faculty or individuals who can provide in-depth evaluation and recommendation. In addition to the faculty letter(s), additional letters may be submitted such as professional mentors, supervisors/employers, physicians you have worked with or shadowed, etc.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
MUSC College of Medicine is privileged to connect with a variety of academically gifted and uniquely talented applicants who share our pursuit of medical excellence, innovation and compassionate service.

The purpose of the Interview Day is to help the Admissions Committee better understand who you are, what matters most to you and why you have chosen to become a physician.

To learn more about the interview process and the Virtual Interview Day, please visit: 
http://medicine.musc.edu/programs/doctor-medicine/admissions/interview-process
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Virtual interviews include 3, one-on-one interviews with a variety of MUSC members (faculty, staff, students, alumni). Interviewees have the opportunity to connect with faculty and current medical students.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Regional physicians (MUSC alumni) assist with virtual interviews.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Virtual interviews will be offered. Please visit the MUSC COM Interview Process for information: https://medicine.musc.edu/programs/doctor-medicine/admissions/interview-process
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Invitations for secondary applications are sent based on specific requirements included on our website: https://medicine.musc.edu/education/medical-students/admissions/criteria
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: South Carolina residents are encouraged to apply Early Decision if they have a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.50 and a minimum MCAT score of 506.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Out-of-State applicants must possess strong Close Ties to South Carolina for interview eligibility. International applicants must be permanent residents of the United State to be considered.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Students who are admitted from out-of-state remain at the out-of-state tuition rate for all four years, with few exceptions.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: As a public, South Carolina medical school, preference is given to in-state residents. Out-of-state applicants must possess strong Close Ties to South Carolina and meet academic minimums.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Applicants holding DACA status may apply to the MD program and be considered for admission to the College of Medicine under the same policies and procedures as other applicants.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The MUSC College of Medicine takes a holistic approach to our selection process.  Adjusted undergraduate cumulative GPA, best MCAT score, experiences, and attributes are equally weighted and are the primary factors when evaluating the competitiveness and potential success of an applicant. 

Please visit our websites for more information:

MUSC COM Selection Criteria: https://medicine.musc.edu/education/medical-students/admissions/criteria
MUSC COM Application Process: https://medicine.musc.edu/education/medical-students/admissions/applying
MUSC COM Application Timeline: https://medicine.musc.edu/education/medical-students/admissions/timeline
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo:
The highest composite MCAT score is factored into an applicant's overall competitiveness. Interviewers do not receive MCAT or total GPA's when interviewing an applicant. 

Admissions Committee members view the entirety of the AMCAS application during Admissions Committee meetings.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo:
South Carolina applicants must have a minimum MCAT of 500 to be considered eligible for interviews.

Out-of-state applicants must meet the average academic thresholds of the current accepted class which consists of a minimum MCAT score of 511 and a cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.7.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo:
South Carolina residents must have a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or a minimum  post-baccalaureate and/or graduate level cumulative GPA of 3.5.

The average accepted undergraduate cumulative GPA is 3.7.

Out-of-State applicants must meet the average academic threshold of the current accepted class which consists of a minimum MCAT score of 511 and a cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.7. Additionally, out-of-state applicants must possess strong “Close Ties to South Carolina”. Out-of-State applicants who do not possess strong “Close Ties to South Carolina,” will not be considered.

See website for more information: https://medicine.musc.edu/education/medical-students/admissions/criteria
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: All postbacc and graduate coursework will be considered as there is no minimum number of credit hours.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo:
Please visit MUSC COM Selection Criteria for more information:
https://medicine.musc.edu/programs/doctor-medicine/admissions/selection-criteria
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of intent and/or unofficial letters of recommendation are not permitted. Only verified Letters of Recommendation submitted through an applicant’s AMCAS application will be considered.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Applicants to the College of Medicine at the Medical University of South Carolina are selected for admission based on their academic, personal, and extracurricular attributes. Applicants must also have the intellectual, physical and emotional capabilities to meet the requirements of the curriculum and of a successful medical career. Final acceptance and matriculation into the College of Medicine is contingent upon the applicant’s ability to satisfy the Technical Standards with or without accommodations.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: A variety of institutional and external scholarships, grants, and loan programs are available for students. Active loan counseling, financial literacy, and debt management programs are in place from pre-enrollment through graduation. Scholarships are awarded by the College of Medicine Scholarship Committee and are based on outstanding academic records, financial need, community engagement, leadership, and personal achievement.

medSchoolMatDemo.matricStateList: Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Massachusetts, New Jersey, North Carolina, South Carolina, Wisconsin

medSchoolPrograms.info: In partnership with the MUSC College of Graduate Studies, students can pursue a MD/Master's in Clinical Research (MD/MSCR) degree as well as a MD/Master's in Public Health (MD/MPHD) degree.

A core mission of the College of Medicine is to support an environment that fosters cultural understanding, cultural competency, and opportunities for individuals of all backgrounds. To support our mission, the PRIME (Pathway Resources & Impactful Mentoring and Excellence) Division works to support all students, residents, and faculty by implementing mentorship and professional development programs designed to ensure we are providing the best health care teams for all South Carolinians.

Our different pathway programs are as follows:

Students Mentors for Minorities in Healthcare (SMH)
Summer Institute*
Summer Medicine Academy
Post-Baccalaureate Reapplication Program (PREP) *
Minorities in Healthcare Mentoring and Advising Through Collaborations in Healthcare (MATCH)

*PREP and Summer Institute programs are available to qualified underrepresented, rural, first generation, and/or socio-economically disadvantaged applicants from SC who have applied, interviewed and been denied admission.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: The Accelerated Medical Pathway (AMP) offers students the opportunity to meet graduation requirements in three years and comes with a directed pathway into one of 8 participating residency programs at MUSC. AMP aligns with MUSC’s mission of retaining trainees for the state’s physician workforce. All students in the MD program complete the same preclerkship curriculum. AMP students  will complete all clerkships, selectives, an AMP selective, and tailored courses during the final enrichment phase.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants:
Students will be eligible for consideration by the Residency Program if they meet all of the following
criteria:
•High academic performance in the preclerkship phase and clinical skills courses.
• Professional behavior with no serious professionalism concerns.
• Behavior consistent with the ability to move through MD degree requirements in an accelerated fashion.

https://musc.policytech.com/dotNet/documents/?docid=11524&app=pt&source=unspecified&public=true
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option for all Three-Year MD students

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: In early April, the waitlist is created and applicants are notified. Not all applicants who interview are placed on the waitlist. Waitlist ranking is not disclosed to applicants.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Although MUSC does not require prerequisite courses, MUSC COM strongly recommends applicants to complete 2 semesters of general biology with lab, general chemistry with lab, organic chemistry with lab, physics with lab, biochemistry with lab, and psychology or social science.  

Other recommendations: anatomy, cell biology, embryology, genetics, and physiology.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: MUSC COM does not have "prerequisites" and encourages candidates to take courses that will help prepare them for the MCAT and medical school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Interview selection is based on the holistic evaluation of an applicant. Though screening for interviews is based on the cumulative undergraduate GPA and best total MCAT score, an applicant's attributes and experiences are equally weighted. Attributes such as critical thinking, cultural competency, emotional intelligence, motivation, oral communication/social skills and principles are assessed in the interview. Experiences such as the quality of recommendations, leadership, volunteer, and shadowing/clinical exposure are also considered. 

MUSC is a public, state-supported institution. Primary preference is given to qualified South Carolina residents. Out-of-state applicants must possess strong Close Ties to South Carolina and have with excellent academics and credentials.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Exposure to medicine and physicians is a requirement for consideration. Medically related experiences (work, volunteer, or shadowing) are expected in order to observe the patient/physician relationship and affirm an interest in medicine. There is no minimum hours required, however,  experiences that are comprehensive and varied are preferred.
